findings.reason: the plan should name death_census.stream_facts (or a shared low-level helper it owns) as the mechanism to extend, so the supervisor and the census cannot disagree about how many records a stream held.
findings.text: §3's `_stream_record_facts` (added at c8f0b545, the plan's §3 node) counts a run's stream records and names the newest record's type by iterating `stream_paths_newest_first`, which is exactly what `reckon/crew/death_census.py::stream_facts` (death_census.py:84, pre-existing since 4ed8ff18c) already computes as `record_count` and `last_record_type` over the same stream files; two scanners of one shape will drift, and the exit record's stream_records_seen / last_record_type fields are the second copy the death census and recovery.py:7009 now read

findings.reason: §10 should extend the owner by calling fleet_supervisor.state_directory / fleet_node.recorded_job_id rather than fork the path resolution and its env override, or the batch step and the dispatcher can resolve different record files.
findings.text: §10's `_fleet_record_path` / `_read_fleet_record` re-derive the fleet record's location (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/…/fleet/record.json` or ~/.local/state/fleet) and read it, while reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py::state_directory (fleet_supervisor.py:253) plus RECORD_NAME (fleet_supervisor.py:83) already own that path and its canonical override FLEET_STATE_DIR, and reckon/crew/fleet_node.py::recorded_job_id (fleet_node.py:299) already performs this exact read; the plan adds a third override RECKON_FLEET_RECORD (dispatch.py:9607) beside FLEET_STATE_DIR/FLEET_RUNTIME_DIR, so the fleet's location now resolves through two independent readers

findings.reason: the justification is recorded in the plan's runpy-warning followup and the module is a single 32-line shim with no duplicated behaviour, so the design already made the call; noting it does not change what the plan does.
findings.text: a whole module exists to forward to `_supervisor_command` and avoids the runpy duplicate-import warning that `-m reckon.crew.dispatch` produced; the plan supplies the reason the existing vector cannot be reused, so this is a justified thin layer rather than a parallel mechanism over the same machinery

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the substantial new behaviour is hidden behind small interfaces. §3's per-run supervisor takes one spec path and is read through three run-directory artifacts; §10's reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py hides the FIFO protocol, the variable-stripping, the mode-0700 runtime directory, the service manager and the zellij tab-sizing behind one request line and serve(). The dilute-launch stages are private helpers inside dispatch.py, but the interface each exposes is small relative to what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 forked the stream-record reader and §10 forked the fleet-record path reader instead of extending their owners, reckon/crew/death_census.py and reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the design searched the transfer layers it names (§10's dotfiles reference, a reuse-map run with 73 resolved citations, and the existing owners it extends: routing._remove_worktree, promotion, summary.roster_bound, resumption, claims._worker_liveness), but it did not search the run's stream/exit readers: §3's exit-record fields stream_records_seen and last_record_type re-derive a scan that reckon/crew/death_census.py::stream_facts already owns, and the plan cites no census reader anywhere.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py is a 32-line module whose whole body forwards to dispatch._supervisor_command, added only so the supervisor is launched as -m reckon.crew.supervisor_main instead of -m reckon.crew.dispatch; the plan does state why the existing launch cannot be reused (runpy re-executes the already-imported dispatch module and opens the supervisor's stderr with a warning), so the wrapper is justified rather than unjustified.
